subject: Finova performance SLOs & multi-region routing — post-call follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>; Priya Singh <priya.singh@finova.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Finova performance SLOs & multi-region routing — post-call recap

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the time this morning — appreciated the deep dive into Finova's latency targets and global routing requirements. Per our call, I wanted to capture the key requirements and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Summary of ask:
- Expected peak throughput: 12k TPS (text-generation tokens) across overall platform during batch settlement windows (~1h).
- Concurrency: ~400 concurrent sessions (web sockets) for real-time customer interactions.
- Latency targets: p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 120ms for short-prompt generation (<= 128 tokens). For longer streaming responses (interactive agents), target tail latency p95 <= 250ms per chunk.
- Streaming: need low-latency token streaming for UI (server-sent events / websockets) with partial-output streaming enabled.
- Regional routing & residency: EU data must remain within EU for EMEA customers. APAC traffic should serve from APAC region where possible; fallback to US only if APAC capacity constrained.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence and audit logs required for procurement; will share SOC2 report and architecture diagram.

Potential Redwood approach (high level):
- Multi-region routing: route by geo with regional model endpoints (us-east, eu-west, ap-southeast). Automatic fallback policy to nearest compatible model instance if capacity is exhausted.
- SLOs: recommend canary + staged rollout. For p95 targets you described, we'll propose a Dedicated pool sized for your peak TPS with conservative concurrency headroom; we can provide an initial latency profile (attached) and an SLO runbook.
- Streaming: use continuous token streaming path with small chunk sizes (8–16 tokens) and KV cache warm-up during bursts to keep p50 low.

Attachments: Finova SLO matrix (attached) includes traffic shape, sample prompts, and suggested Dedicated sizing. Also attached is a short Redwood latency profile for reference.

Next steps / owners:
- Aditya (SE): follow up with a short perf validation plan and sample config for Dedicated pool sizing — target by EOD Tue.
- Finova: can you confirm which EU countries require strict residency vs. those acceptable to be routed to eu-west? Also confirm if APAC can accept US fallback or if strict residency is required there too.
- Marissa: schedule technical deep-dive + perf workshop (45–60m) next week.

If that looks right I’ll send calendar invites and the perf plan.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Finova performance SLOs & multi-region routing — post-call recap

Hi Marissa — thanks for the detailed recap. This aligns with our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Latency definitions — when you call p95 <= 120ms, is that end-to-end server-side token generation time (excludes network to client) or client-observed RTT including network? For procurement we need to be explicit.

2) Streaming: for the interactive agent flows we need chunk latency (time between first token and subsequent chunks) to be <= 200ms at p95. Is that feasible with the chunk sizes you recommended?

3) Residency: EU strict residency applies to customers based in Germany and France (data must remain in EU). APAC is mixed; for Australia we need residency, but Japan/SEA can accept APAC-hosted with US fallback during incidents.

4) Can you share a rough cost estimate for Dedicated pools to meet the above (ballpark)? We understand this will be an estimate but need it for initial procurement planning.

Thanks — if Aditya can run through the perf validation plan that would be great. Priya — looping you for procurement visibility.

--
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering, Finova
alex.johnson@finova.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-13T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finova performance SLOs & multi-region routing — post-call recap

Alex — quick answers and a pragmatic validation plan. Happy to go deeper on the technical call.

1) Latency definition: We report server-side generation latency (time from request arrival at Redwood edge to token generation). For client-observed latency we'll add network RTT delta in the doc, but procurement p95 targets should specify whether they want server-side p95 or end-to-end. I recommend server-side p95 <= 120ms and a separate network budget.

2) Streaming chunk latency: 200ms p95 is achievable with chunk sizes of 8–12 tokens and a Dedicated instance with low-variance kernels (we'll enable prioritized scheduling for those sessions). Key to hitting p95 is kernel selection and warm KV cache. We'll include warm-up scripts in the perf plan.

3) Residency & routing: we can enforce region-locked endpoints for Germany/France and Australia. For Japan/SEA we can use APAC region endpoints with a documented fallback to US in incident scenarios. We'll add routing policy examples (geo match + customer tag).

4) Ballpark Dedicated sizing / cost: based on the traffic shape in the attached matrix (12k TPS peak over 1h with 400 concurrent RT sessions), initial recommended config: 6 dedicated GPUs (A100-class or equivalent) in each primary region (US/EU/APAC) with autoscale headroom; rough monthly run-rate estimate: $55k–$80k per region depending on exact instance/commit. I'll formalize this into a short estimate and include currency breakout.

Perf validation plan (high level):
- Day 0: synthetic workload runner (we'll provide script + sample prompts).
- Day 1: run peak traffic with KV cold/warm scenarios; measure p50/p95/p99 and chunk latency.
- Day 2: run geo-failover test (APAC -> US fallback) and measure tail impact.
- Deliverable: perf report with config recommendations and SLO targets.

I'll attach a short perf-run checklist in a follow-up and propose Wed/Thu next week for a 60m technical workshop.

—Aditya
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
